answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring a costly, verifiable stake before participation: each agent must lock a bond and build a public reputation history, like a raven that earns trust by returning to the same roost night after night. New identities start with a violet badge that marks them as unproven, so counterparties discount their offers until they accumulate honest work. Past fraud becomes a permanent relic on the ledger, a public record peers can check before trading, making it expensive to abandon a stained identity and start fresh.
